title: Benny Safdie’s ‘Lizard Music’ With Dwayne Johnson Adds Newcomer Arya Parvathi (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Benny Safdie’s upcoming fantasy movie “Lizard Music” has added newcomer Arya Parvathi in her feature film debut.

	Parvathi’s role has yet to be dis
body:
Benny Safdie’s upcoming fantasy movie “Lizard Music” has added newcomer Arya Parvathi in her feature film debut.

	Parvathi’s role has yet to be disclosed, but she joins a cast that includes Dwayne Johnson (playing a 70-year-old man whose best friend is a 111-year-old chicken), Alicia Silverstone, Regina Hall, Tim Heidecker and Theo Leber. Safdie directs and wrote the script, which is based on the Daniel Pinkwater novel of the same name. 
	

	“Lizard Music” follows a boy (Leber) who, left to his own devices, stumbles upon a secret late-night broadcast of lizards playing otherworldly music. His exploration into this magical world leads him to an eccentric old man called the Chicken Man (Johnson), and his elderly chicken companion Claudia. Per the logline, “United by this shared vision, they set off on an adventure that begins as a hunt for a hidden society but blossoms into something far greater: a voyage through invisible worlds, unexpected harmonies, and the unbreakable bond between lost souls who discover magic not only in what they find, but in each other.”


	The film is produced by Scott Stuber and Nick Nesbitt for United Artists; Safdie for Out for the Count Productions; Johnson for Seven Bucks Productions; and David Koplan for Magnetic Fields Entertainment.

	Parvathi makes her feature film debut in “Lizard Music.” She recently appeared in a live theater production of “Commedia Robots” at the Actors’ Gang theater in Culver City, as well as a short film produced by The Playground young actors’ conservatory in Los Angeles. She is represented by CESD and Horizon Talent Mgmt.

schema.headline: Benny Safdie’s ‘Lizard Music’ With Dwayne Johnson Adds Newcomer Arya Parvathi (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Sam Fender and Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ Becomes the U.K.’s Longest-Running No. 1 Single of All Time
description:
Sam Fender and Olivia Dean are making U.K. chart history.

	Their collaborative single, “Rein Me In,” has officially become the country’s longest-ru
body:
Sam Fender and Olivia Dean are making U.K. chart history.

	Their collaborative single, “Rein Me In,” has officially become the country’s longest-running No. 1 single of all time. With 19 weeks at the top of the U.K. Official Singles chart, it has officially surpassed the record set by Frankie Laine’s “I Believe,” which held the spot for 18 weeks back in 1953. 

	But this isn’t the first record the duet has broken. Released over a year ago on June 20, 2025, “Rein Me In” took 35 weeks from its first entry onto the chart to reach No. 1, making it the song with the longest climb to the top. Since it hit that spot in February, “Rein Me In” has also become Fender’s first U.K. No. 1 single and the only single in U.K. chart history that has bumped back to No. 1 four times in the same run. 
	

	“This is a historic achievement,” said Ben Mortimer, president of Polydor Label Group, where Fender is signed. “The accolades have continued to grow throughout this incredible journey, but to surpass a benchmark set by the great Frankie Laine more than 70 years ago is almost unimaginable. Seeing Sam and Olivia, two homegrown stars, break the record is something we’re so proud of.”


	Added Jo Charrington, the president of Capitol U.K., where Dean is signed: “There is something completely undeniable about Sam and Olivia together on this record. They created a song that people have continued to return to week after week. To see that connection translate into the longest No.1 run in the history of the U.K. chart is a landmark achievement.”

schema.headline: Sam Fender and Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ Becomes the U.K.’s Longest-Running No. 1 Single of All Time

title: Samara Weaving to Play Emma Frost in Marvel’s ‘X-Men’ Reboot
description:
Samara Weaving will move from “Ready or Not” to the MCU. 

	The Australian actress has been cast in Marvel’s reboot of “The X-Men.” Weaving will pla
body:
Samara Weaving will move from “Ready or Not” to the MCU. 

	The Australian actress has been cast in Marvel’s reboot of “The X-Men.” Weaving will play Emma Frost, who in comics lore has moved from supervillain to superhero over the course of the mutant’s long, long run in print. Telepathy is her jam.

	A rep for Weaving declined to comment, and a rep for Marvel did not respond to a request for comment.


	The casting comes after Marvel unveiled a big Hall H presentation at Comic-Con last weekend, introducing Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider and revealing that “Alien: Romulus” actor David Jonsson will take over the mantle as the king of Wakanda in “Black Panther 3.” After being the most successful brand in movies, Marvel has struggled at the box office, with recent films like “Captain America: Brave New World” and “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” disappointing. However, this weekend’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is expected to turn things around and is already shattering records. Sony distributes those films.
	

	Weaving most recently appeared in “Ready or Not 2: Here I Come” and “Over Your Dead Body.” Other credits include “The Babysitter,” “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” “Scream VI” and “Bill & Ted Face the Music.” “The X-Men” will be directed by Jake Schreier, who oversaw last year’s “Thunderbolts.”

	The mutant heroes, at least the ones from the 20th Century Fox films, will pop up in “Avengers: Doomsday” with the likes of Ian McKellen, Patrick Stewart and James Marsden appearing in the gangs-all-here mashup. Disney, which owns Marvel, acquired Fox in 2019 and with it the rights to integrate the Marvel heroes it had licensed to the studio into the MCU. 
	

	Deadline broke the news about Weaving’s casting. Weaving is represented by CAA and 111 Media.

schema.headline: Samara Weaving to Play Emma Frost in Marvel’s ‘X-Men’ Reboot

title: Brent Lang Named Editor-in-Chief of IndieWire
description:
Variety‘s Brent Lang has been named the new editor-in-chief of IndieWire, effective August 17. 

	Based in New York City, Lang will report to Jerry
body:
Variety‘s Brent Lang has been named the new editor-in-chief of IndieWire, effective August 17. 

	Based in New York City, Lang will report to Jerry Ruiz, senior vice president, operations & finance, PMC. A widely respected journalist and editor, Lang brings a distinctive combination of editorial leadership, industry expertise, and a deep commitment to ambitious, high-quality storytelling to IndieWire. 


	Lang most recently served as executive editor of Variety, where he covered the major Hollywood studios and their corporate parents. During his tenure, he wrote cover stories on many of the industry’s most notable figures, including Christopher Nolan, Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Kevin Hart, George Clooney, Mindy Kaling, Michelle Williams, Michael J. Fox and Benedict Cumberbatch.
	

	Since joining Variety in 2014 as a senior film and media reporter, Lang rose through a series of leadership roles, including New York bureau chief and executive editor, film and media. 

	In 2024, he was named entertainment journalist of the year by the Los Angeles Press Club. 

	Before Variety, Lang was a senior reporter at TheWrap, and his work has also appeared in The Patriot-Ledger, The Providence Journal, CBSNews.com and Forbes. He is a graduate of Brown University and the Columbia University School of Journalism. 

	“Brent is a dynamic and deeply respected editor whose experience, instincts, and creativity make him exceptionally well-suited to lead IndieWire,” said Ruiz. “He brings a sophisticated understanding of the entertainment industry, a strong editorial point of view, and a clear sense of where media is headed. Just as importantly, he understands what has always made IndieWire unique with its intelligence, its authority, and its commitment to championing bold voices and original storytelling. We are thrilled to welcome Brent to IndieWire and excited for the future of the brand under his leadership.” 
	

	“I’m deeply honored to take the editorial helm of a brand I’ve admired for many years,” said Lang. “IndieWire has long stood for smart, distinctive, and fearless journalism, and it has built an extraordinary legacy by championing artists, elevating emerging voices, and covering the industry with depth and conviction. I have enormous respect for IndieWire’s founder, Eugene Hernandez, and for Dana Harris-Bridson’s profound contributions. They are responsible for building a world-class brand. I’m also incredibly grateful to Jay Penske, Michelle Sobrino, Dea Lawrence, Ramin Setoodeh and Cynthia Littleton for the opportunities they have given me over the years. At a time of great change across media and entertainment, I believe there is tremendous opportunity ahead for a brand that has always believed in bold ideas, fresh perspectives and the enduring power of great storytelling.” 

	Lang succeeds Dana Harris-Bridson, whose 15 years of editorial leadership helped to shape IndieWire into the expansive and highly regarded brand it is today. During her tenure, IndieWire broadened its focus beyond independent film into television, blockbusters and the crafts that define the industry, while also launching standout editorial franchises including Future of Filmmaking and the In Development newsletter.

	Harris-Bridson is stepping down to focus on building her own projects, an exciting next chapter that reflects both the depth of her experience and her genuine desire to devote her time and energy to work she’s passionate about. 

	“Dana has been instrumental in shaping IndieWire into the exceptional brand it is today,” said Ruiz. “Her leadership, editorial vision, and deep commitment to the brand have left a lasting mark on IndieWire and on the many people who have had the opportunity to work alongside her. We are deeply grateful for all she has contributed and for the strong foundation she leaves behind.” 

	“Dana’s contributions to IndieWire have been extraordinary,” said James Israel, publisher of IndieWire. “Her leadership helped shape the brand’s editorial identity, expand its reach, and strengthen its standing within the entertainment community. We are deeply grateful for all she has done to help build IndieWire into what it is today. At the same time, I’m excited to work alongside Brent as we begin this next chapter and continue building on that foundation with energy, ambition, and optimism for what lies ahead.” 
	

	“It’s been the privilege of my career to help lead this team and this brand to where it is today,” said Harris-Bridson. “I’m proud of everything we built together, and I’m energized by what’s next.” 

	The transition comes at a moment of strong momentum for IndieWire. The brand recently earned two Daytime Emmy Award nominations for its inaugural Craft Roundtables series, and Lynne Howard was recently promoted to senior vice president of operations, reporting to James Israel. Together, these leadership appointments reflect IndieWire’s continued growth, as well as a shared commitment to the values that have long defined the brand: bold journalism, authoritative storytelling, and an enduring belief in the power of original voices and ambitious editorial vision.

schema.headline: Brent Lang Named Editor-in-Chief of IndieWire

title: AI Studio Asteria, Co-Founded by Natasha Lyonne, Strikes Strategic Partnership with Virtual Production Studio ZeroSpace (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Asteria, the AI studio co-founded by filmmaker Bryn Mooser and Natasha Lyonne, has struck a strategic partnership with ZeroSpace, a virtual producti
body:
Asteria, the AI studio co-founded by filmmaker Bryn Mooser and Natasha Lyonne, has struck a strategic partnership with ZeroSpace, a virtual production studio, in the hopes of transforming hybrid models of filmmaking.

	The partnership between the two coastal studios — Asteria is based in Los Angeles, while ZeroSpace is based in Brooklyn, New York — aims to streamline the filmmaking process by developing new hybrid production workflows and physical facilities to help filmmakers move through different elements of a production, including story development, visual effects and virtual production (ala those involving the Volume) itself. 
	

	The two companies will also work together on original productions, research initiatives and education programs, while giving ZeroSpace access to Asteria’s suite of products, such as its AI operating system Continuum. The deal also gives Asteria access to ZeroGen, ZeroSpace’s generative AI platform that aims to let studios generate content within legal guidelines, helping enterprise customers avoid the legally murky areas of copyright issues.


	“Virtual production transformed where movies could be made. The next transformation is who can wield the technology to make them,” said Asteria CEO Benjamin Michel, another co-founder. “We believe the future is hybrid production, where the latest generative technology works in concert with tactile filmmaking, utilizing actors, cinematographers, production designers, VFX artists and the like. This isn’t about automating away artists or making productions cheaper; it’s about giving filmmakers the ability to tell stories that were once out of reach, letting the technology disappear into the creative process so their vision reaches the screen more fully than ever. ZeroSpace has built one of the world’s leading virtual production facilities, and we’re excited to build that future together.”
	

	“ZeroSpace was built on the idea that technology should remove barriers between imagination and execution,” ZeroSpace CEO and foudner Jon Kreutzer said. “Asteria shares that vision. Together, we’re exploring how virtual production and AI-enabled creative tools can expand what’s creatively possible while keeping filmmakers and artists firmly at the center of the process. The goal isn’t to change who tells stories. It’s to give storytellers more powerful ways to bring their visions to life.”

schema.headline: AI Studio Asteria, Co-Founded by Natasha Lyonne, Strikes Strategic Partnership with Virtual Production Studio ZeroSpace (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Mahershala Ali Calls Out Marvel for Not Making ‘Blade’: ‘You Had Me Under Contract. They Have Billions of Dollars. If They Wanted to Do It, We Would’ve Done It’
description: As most Marvel fans know by now, Mahershala Ali was announced to star in a “Blade” movie during a flashy, surprise Comic-Con appearance in 2019, but
body:
As most Marvel fans know by now, Mahershala Ali was announced to star in a “Blade” movie during a flashy, surprise Comic-Con appearance in 2019, but the movie didn’t get made. The two-time Oscar winner never appeared in live-action as the popular vampire-hunting anti-hero, despite Marvel Studios hiring director Bassam Tariq, and later Yann Demange, to helm the film.

	Now after production stalled out, Ali and Tariq have teamed up in the wake of the failed Marvel movie to make this fall’s Amazon MGM action film, “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother.” If the actor and director hadn’t been brought together for “Blade,” their new movie wouldn’t have been made.
	

	“When I look at this and ‘Blade,’ I couldn’t have done both, and the reason this even exists is because that project fell apart and Bassam had the time, space, energy, and focus to go and write this and then re-approach me,” Ali told GQ. “And I was able to use those skills that I had been working on for over a year training for ‘Blade.’ In that way, I feel creatively redeemed on some level, just in my own journey between me, myself, and I.”


	Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige, who announced Ali’s casting as Blade at Comic-Con seven years ago, recently spoke openly about his personal disappointment at the movie not getting made.

	“I am feeling like a gigantic loser and failure that we didn’t get off the ground with Mahershala,” Feige said on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast last week. “We didn’t want to simply just put a leather outfit on him and have him start killing vampires. It had to be unique. It fell into the time when we started pulling back and saying, ‘Only accept insanely great.’ And it wasn’t ‘insanely great’ at the time. We didn’t feel like, as we often do, you can have a good script and make it a great script through production. We didn’t feel confident that we could do that on ‘Blade,’ and we didn’t want to do that to Mahershala and didn’t want to do that to us.”
	

	Ultimately, Ali is happy that he’s starring in “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother” instead of “Blade.”

	“When I look at what is for me, is it was either this or that — and I’ll take this. No offense to them. I’ve been doing this professionally for pushing 30 years now, and one thing I’ve learned is that what is for you is for you and what is not is not. For whatever reason, that project is not for me. If they wanted to do it, we would’ve done it. So I have to move on, and I have moved on,” he said. “Again, you had me under contract, they have billions of dollars, if they wanted to do the movie, we would’ve done the movie. So we’re not doing the movie.”

	Last week at San Diego Comic-Con, Feige announced a “Ghost Rider” movie starring Ryan Gosling and “Black Panther 3,” starring David Jonsson as the new hero.

schema.headline: Mahershala Ali Calls Out Marvel for Not Making ‘Blade’: ‘You Had Me Under Contract. They Have Billions of Dollars. If They Wanted to Do It, We Would’ve Done It’

title: ‘Obsession’ Star Inde Navarrette Confirms Meeting With ‘X-Men’ Director Jake Schreier and Would Love to Play Mystique
description: After “Obsession” became an unprecedented box office success and earned over $400 million from a small budget, all eyes are on breakout star Inde Na
body:
After “Obsession” became an unprecedented box office success and earned over $400 million from a small budget, all eyes are on breakout star Inde Navarrette. 

	“I’ve been taking a lot of meetings since ‘Obsession’ came out,” she explained on Variety’s “Up Next” podcast. “That’s been really nice because you get to meet people and ask questions.”

	One of those meetings, as one might expect for one of Hollywood’s rising stars, was with Marvel Studios. Navarrette revealed she recently met with “Thunderbolts” director Jake Schreier, who is now developing Marvel’s upcoming “X-Men” film. She said she grew up watching Fox’s original 2000s “X-Men” movies and praised Schreier for bringing back the character-driven storytelling that she loved about that era of Marvel.
	

	“I thought what Jake brought to ‘Thunderbolts’ was what I used to love about Marvel,” Navarrette said. “It was character-driven, and the whole time I just couldn’t stop yapping about how much I appreciated what he did with Marvel.”While the “Obsession” star stopped short of revealing more about her conversation with Schreier, she tempered expectations by explaining that many of her recent meetings have simply been opportunities to meet filmmakers she admires, whether or not they lead to a contract being signed.

	“That’s kind of the luxury I have right now, meeting all these different kinds of people,” she said. “Not all of those meetings turn into projects, but sometimes it’s just, ‘I really want to work with you. I’ve seen this project, and this one, and this one.’”Several of the legacy “X-Men” actors, including Patrick Stewart’s Professor Xavier, Ian McKellen’s Magneto, James Marsden’s Cyclops, Kelsey Grammer’s Beast, Alan Cumming’s Nightcrawler and Rebecca Romijn’s shape-shifter Mystique will appear in “Avengers: Doomsday” this December.

	Following “Avengers: Secret Wars” in 2027, which will likely bring back even more legacy Marvel performers, Kevin Feige’s Marvel universe will start anew with a younger group of X-Men in Schreier’s upcoming film. Presumably, Sadie Sink’s Jean Gray (just introduced in Marvel and Sony’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day”) will be one of the leading stars of the film.
	

	As for what character Navarrette could play, she left fans with a tease: “I mean, Mystique has always been super cool.”

schema.headline: ‘Obsession’ Star Inde Navarrette Confirms Meeting With ‘X-Men’ Director Jake Schreier and Would Love to Play Mystique

title: Meghann Fahy to Lead HBO Limited Series ‘Trial of Louise Woodward’ From Matthew Barry, Susanne Bier
description:
HBO has ordered the limited series “The Trial of Louise Woodward” with Meghann Fahy attached to play the lead role. 

	The five-episode series is ba
body:
HBO has ordered the limited series “The Trial of Louise Woodward” with Meghann Fahy attached to play the lead role. 

	The five-episode series is based on a true story. Matthew Barry (“Industry,” “The Guest) serves as writer, executive producer, and showrunner. Susanne Bier (“Practical Magic 2,” “The Night Manager”) is attached to direct all episodes and executive produce. It is slated to premiere in 2027. 


	The logline for the project states that it tells the “shocking true story of how, in 1997, an 18-year-old British au pair was accused of shaking to death a baby left in her care by her American host family, setting off an international media firestorm as the trial unfolds in full view of both the British and American public.” 
	

	“We are thrilled to partner with Matthew Barry and Susanne Bier on this new series and to welcome Meghann Fahy back to the HBO family,” said Francesca Orsi, executive vice president of HBO Programming and head of HBO Drama Series and Films. “Matthew’s compassionate approach to this gripping true story, paired with Susanne’s powerfully distinct directorial vision and Meghann’s exceptional talent, has brought together an extraordinary creative team whose work we’re excited to share with our audience soon.” 

	Along with Barry and Bier, Big Light Productions founder Frank Spotnitz will serve as executive producer alongside Emily Feller, Tobi de Graaff, and Antoine Douaihy. 

	“The trial of Louise Woodward raised profound questions about childcare, working mothers, class, and the role of an emerging 24/7 media,” Barry said. “Thirty years later, those questions feel more urgent and relevant than ever. I’m grateful to be working with Susanne and our partners at HBO to bring this story, in all its complexity, to the screen.” 
	

	Fahy received an Emmy nomination in 2023 for her role in Season 2 of HBO’s hit series “The White Lotus.” She received her second Emmy nod in 2025 for the Netflix series “Sirens.” She is best known for starring in the Freeform drama “The Bold Type,” starring in that show throughout its five-season run at the basic cabler. Her film roles include “Drop” and “Burning Bodhi.” 

	Fahy is repped by WME, Anonymous Content, and Sloane Offer. Barry is repped by The Agency and WME. Bier is repped by CAA, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, and Jackoway Austin Tyerman.

schema.headline: Meghann Fahy to Lead HBO Limited Series ‘Trial of Louise Woodward’ From Matthew Barry, Susanne Bier

title: Olivia Wilde’s ‘The Invite’ Nears $40 Million Globally, Becoming a Rare Hit Summer Comedy
description:
Olivia Wilde’s “The Invite” has become one of today’s rare indie comedies to connect at the summer box office.

	Sandwiched between big-budget block
body:
Olivia Wilde’s “The Invite” has become one of today’s rare indie comedies to connect at the summer box office.

	Sandwiched between big-budget blockbusters like “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” A24‘s “The Invite” has climbed to $20 million in North America and $15.7 million internationally from 36 markets after three weekends in wide release. Thanks to stellar reviews and even better word-of-mouth, ticket sales are about to surpass $40 million worldwide — and that’s before the movie has opened in all overseas territories. It has yet to debut in key countries like Italy, France and Spain.
	

	“It’s holding up nicely in the U.S., and it still has a lot of key dates in Europe ahead,” says David A. Gross, who runs the movie consulting firm Franchise Entertainment Research. “I would not be surprised if it finished with over $60 million worldwide — that’s excellent.”


	Of course, this summer’s “Obsession” ($262 million domestically, $459 million globally) and “Backrooms” ($196 million domestically, $389 million globally) were massive, paradigm-shifting successes in the arthouse space. But outside of horror, few independent releases have managed to surpass the $20 million mark at the domestic box office since COVID upended the movie theater industry. Others this year include A24’s dramedy “The Drama” starring Zendaya and Robert Pattinson ($48 million domestically, $132 million globally), YouTuber Mark Fischbach’s self-distributed “Iron Lung” ($40 million domestically, $50 million globally) and two Angel Studios offerings, the romantic comedy “Solo Mio” with Kevin James ($25 million domestically) and historical drama “Young Washington” ($45 million).
	

	“The Invite,” starring Wilde, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton, was one of the biggest sales out of Sundance, with A24 nabbing domestic rights for $12 million. As the movie was sparking a bidding war, Wilde pushed for a traditional theatrical release. Her instinct was spot on, because 90% of opening weekend audiences recommended seeing “The Invite” on the big screen rather than at home, according to PostTrak exit polls. Written by Rashida Jones and Will McCormack and adapted from the Spanish film “The People Upstairs,” the ensemble comedy plays out during a dinner party with a couple going through a rough patch and their free-spirited neighbors. Wilde labored on “The Invite” for six years, dealing with delays from the 2023 actors and writers strike and devastating 2024 Los Angeles wildfires, as well as a complete cast turnover. Amy Adams, Paul Rudd and Tessa Thompson were originally set to star but departed as development stalled. 

	“I’m grateful to see the communal experience of a comedy back in theaters — one that also resonates in a deeply emotional and heartfelt way,” says David Permut, who produced “The Invite” with Annapurna’s Megan Ellison and Ben Browning. “I think it’s what people crave; it’s something that has been missing at the box office for some time now, and the success shows the demand is there.”

	For a crowd-pleaser like “The Invite,” A24 opted for a platform release, a method of distribution that indie studios have mostly abandoned since the pandemic got older audiences out of the moviegoing habit. A platform release involves opening a movie in select theaters, usually in New York City and Los Angeles, and slowly expanding to more cities before launching nationwide. It’s a way to build awareness and generate buzz for something that’s not yet familiar to the masses. Although “The Invite” skews younger than the traditional arthouse release, with a quarter of the audience below the age of 25 and the majority around 35 years old, Gross believes the platform strategy “makes sense for this film.”

	“Reviews and word-of-mouth are outstanding, but they need time to circulate,” Gross says. “That’s what’s driving business now going into the fourth weekend of wide release.”

	Since indies like “The Drama,” “Backrooms” and “Obsession” opened nationwide from the start, “The Invite” stands as the best platform release of the year. Others to attempt the limited-release strategy include Black Bear’s crime thriller “Tuner” ($4.5 million domestically), A24’s BDSM drama “Pillion” ($3 million domestically), Lionsgate’s musical comedy “Power Ballad” ($2.6 million domestically) and Magnolia’s satire “Maddie’s Secret” ($1.1 million).
	

	“The Invite” is also the second-highest-grossing summer platform release since COVID, trailing only Wes Anderson’s sci-fi dramedy “Asteroid City,” which earned $28.1 million domestically and $53 million worldwide. Arthouse movies weren’t always a rarity during popcorn season; beloved hits like “Little Miss Sunshine,” “The Big Sick,” “Blue Jasmine,” “Boyhood,” “500 Days of Summer” and “The Kids Are All Right” all released as counterprogramming before the dog days of summer. Nowadays, studios prefer to save their awards fare for fall and winter so they’re fresh in the minds of voters. But recent Oscar winners like Ryan Coogler’s “Sinners,” the Daniels’ “Everything Everywhere All at Once” and Christopher Nolan’s “Oppenheimer” premiered on the big screen months removed from traditional awards season launching pads, giving A24 confidence that quality movies can succeed at any time of year.

	“Indie films don’t have to conquer the summer,” says analyst Jeff Bock of Exhibitor Relations. “Sometimes success means finding the audience the blockbusters weren’t serving.”

	“The Invite” is Wilde’s third directorial effort following 2019’s well-reviewed comedy “Booksmart,” which generated $25 million globally against a $6 million budget, and 2023’s provocative drama “Don’t Worry Darling,” which grossed $87 million against a $35 million budget. She’s starring in another summer indie, Magnolia’s erotic thriller “I Want Your Sex,” which opens over the weekend. If Tom Holland and Zendaya, who star in “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” are the king and queen of the summer blockbuster, Wilde might just be the titan of the indies.

schema.headline: Olivia Wilde’s ‘The Invite’ Nears $40 Million Globally, Becoming a Rare Hit Summer Comedy

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Craze Continues as New BFI Imax Screenings Sell Out in Under 30 Minutes (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
London’s BFI Imax cinema — the biggest Imax screen in the U.K. — is experiencing its very own Odyssey. 

	On Friday, due to unprecedented demand to
body:
London’s BFI Imax cinema — the biggest Imax screen in the U.K. — is experiencing its very own Odyssey. 

	On Friday, due to unprecedented demand to see Chris Nolan’s already record-breaking “The Odyssey,” on Imax 70mm, as the director intended, the BFI Imax released another batch of tickets. 

	However, seemingly only those with the gods on their side got lucky. Within minutes of going on sale at 2 p.m. local time, there were reports of them having already sold out, with stories appearing online about “40,000 people” being in a virtual queue. The BFI later told Variety that all tickets had gone “in under 30 minutes.”
	

	“Odysseus waited 10 years to get home. These fans are about to wait longer just to sit down,” wrote one social media user. 


	The latest sell-out of tickets comes just weeks after “The Odyssey” became the BFI Imax’s biggest opening weekend of all time, taking £219,867 ($300,000) over three days and topping “Star Wars: The Last Jedi.”

	The film also broke the theater’s single-day pre-sale record, selling 28,000 tickets in 24 hours a full year in advance, amounting to a £750,000 ($1 million) in gross revenue. That surpassed the pre-sale record for “Dune: Part Two” and “Oppenheimer,” which took £366,000 and £254,000 respectively in their first 24 hours on sale.

	But one cinema in London offers just a snapshot of the global phenomenon that “The Odyssey” has become, with the film recently surpassing $700 million to become the fourth highest-grossing movie of the year after just 12 days in theaters.

	For a short period, it did seem that the U.K. did have one over the U.S., where there were numerous complaints about AMC’s website crashing after new tickets went on sale. However, it would soon emerge on Friday that the BFI’s website, much like Odysseus’s plans to make it back home from Troy to see his wife Penelope in decent time, had also crashed.

schema.headline: ‘The Odyssey’ Craze Continues as New BFI Imax Screenings Sell Out in Under 30 Minutes (EXCLUSIVE)

            A jet ski operator is lucky to be alive after he slammed into a dock at full throttle ... and it seems a particularly difficult stunt caused all of the problems.
      
    
            Dillan Stapler -- a jet ski influencer who is part of the "Lanier Crew," a group of jet skiers based out of Georgia -- shared a video of himself running straight into a dock.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Check it out ... he crashed at full speed and is jettisoned off the jet ski -- landing in a heap on the unforgiving wood.
      

            Stapler's pulls him from the water ... and he looks totally lifeless -- held above water only by his life vest and his pal.
      
    
          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            Stapler explains on TikTok he apparently passed out after climbing onto the front of his jet ski to operate it from the vehicle's "hood." Video taken from behind shows him go limp ... and he's lucky he didn't fall off and get dragged under the jet ski.
      
    
            He says this goes to show even professionals need to be careful ... after all, jet skis may look like toys -- but they go pretty darn fast!

            North West has pulled the plug on two of her upcoming tour dates, days before she was scheduled to hit the stage, TMZ has learned.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            North was all set to hit the stage for her first performance on August 5 with rapper Molly Santana in Dallas, Texas. But, according to Ticketmaster, the show is now canceled along with their August 17 concert in Toronto, Canada.
      
    
            Not only that, but the official website promoting the artists' "Kimokawaii" tour has apparently been scrubbed from the Internet. The only good news is that their August 25 show at San Francisco's "The Midway" is still listed on the venue's site ... for now.
      
    
            As you know, North is the 13-year-old daughter of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. The Kardashian clan has been super supportive of North's music career, posting Instagram photos that show them grooving to North's new album, which was released in May. 
      
    
            We've reached out to reps for North and Santana ... so far, no word back.

title: Brittney Griner Files For Divorce From Wife After 8 Years of Marriage
description:
Brittney Griner
                          Files For Divorce From Wife Cherelle
body:
Brittney Griner
                          Files For Divorce From Wife Cherelle
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 31, 2026
                            9:33 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  July 31, 2026
                                10:17 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brittney Griner has filed for divorce from her wife, Cherelle -- the woman who stood by her when she was locked up in Russia -- after eight years of marriage.
      
    
            The WNBA star filed the divorce petition Thursday ... and lists July 24 as the date of separation. She says their marriage is "irretrievably broken."
      
    
            Brittney and Cherelle -- who share one child together -- tied the knot back in June of 2018 ... and remained together during the 10 months Brittney spent in a Russian prison.
      

            Brittney's asking the court for joint legal custody and to determine how much child support to award, if any at all.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            While Brittney balls up the basketball court, Cherelle dominates the court of law ... she's an attorney and was a leading advocate in pushing for Brittney's release from Russia back in late 2022, months after she was sentenced to 9 years in a Russian prison for allegedly possessing marijuana.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cherelle told People that she felt "hopeless" during Brittney's prison sentence ... and she told them all about their tearful reunion.
      
    
            Griner -- a 9-time WNBA all-star -- is averaging a team-high 14.1 points per game with the Connecticut Sun this season.
